open.narrate: Boots of every size stand by the orchard gate, and somebody has strung lanterns between the trees.

open.line: I brought the long table from the shop. You lot need a bigger one now.

9000001.line: I planted a row of beans for every name at this table, {farmer}. Count them later.

9000002.line: The lanterns were my idea. The ladder was not.

9000003.line: It's loud. I like it. Don't tell anyone I said that.

close.narrate: The lanterns burn down one by one, and nobody hurries home, because home is right here.

open.narrate: Rain on the porch roof. The whole household squeezed under one awning, and still room for the kettle.

open.line: When I kept this farm it was me and a goat. Look at it now.

9000001.line: Rain's good for the rows. And for sitting close.

9000002.line: I counted the mugs. We need more mugs, {farmer}.

9000003.line: The pond will be full tomorrow. I'll catch breakfast for everyone.

close.narrate: The rain stops before anyone notices. Nobody moves for a while anyway.

open.narrate: From the Overlook the homestead's roofs make a little village of their own, smoke rising from every chimney.

open.line: The town council asked me what to call this end of the valley. I said I'd ask you.

9000001.line: Call it home. It's what we say anyway.

9000002.line: Fifteen roofs, and I've fixed the gutters on all of them.

9000003.line: From up here it looks small. It isn't. It's the biggest thing I have.

close.narrate: The Mayor writes something down, crosses it out, and writes "Home" instead.

9000001: Kettle's on. You sleep like a fallen fence post, {farmer}.
I already watered the porch pots. Sit, have the good cup.
The rows can wait ten minutes. Stay.
9000002: I found a nest in the gutter. We're keeping it.
Breakfast is whatever I find on the way back from the woods.

open.narrate: The whole valley comes up the festival road for the Great Harvest. Every table is borrowed and every lantern lit.

open.line: Twenty weddings on one farm. The town's never seen a harvest like it, and neither have I.

9000001.line: First row I ever planted was beside yours. Every row since, too.

9000002.line: I wove the crowns for the tables. Yours has the most acorns. On purpose.

9000003.line: I thought the quiet was what I wanted. Then you all happened.

close.narrate: The music goes on past midnight. Somewhere in it, the whole household is dancing at once.

close.line: Same time next year, then. The farm's not done yet.
